findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued is fixed at import time
findings.body: AssignmentSource.queued is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class body runs, not when each instance is created, and datetime is immutable so this does not raise the mutable-default error. Every AssignmentSource built by from_integration (the inbound webhook path) or by from_dict when queued is omitted therefore shares one timestamp: the moment this module was imported in that process, not when the assignment was queued. to_dict()/asdict() copies that stale value into the Celery kwargs for sync_assignee_outbound, so task payloads carry a misleading queue time. The cycle check does not read queued today, but the field cannot be used to order or drop the rapid assignee updates this change is about, and debugging those races from the payload will be wrong. tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py only asserts queued is not None, so it does not catch this. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now). Also, to_dict() emits the raw datetime and from_dict() will not parse an ISO string back into a datetime, so the dict is only safe if the task serializer preserves datetime objects.

findings.title: Inbound webhook cycle-break path is untested
findings.body: The production fix attaches AssignmentSource inside sync_group_assignee_inbound on both assign (line 115) and deassign (line 98), then relies on the outbound task to skip the originating integration. The only new test, test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration, calls GroupAssignee.objects.assign directly with an AssignmentSource and never goes through sync_group_assignee_inbound. The existing inbound tests call that function but do not run tasks or assert that outbound sync is skipped. Deleting the new assignment_source arguments from the inbound entry point would leave CI green and the Jira echo loop intact. There is also no test that a second, different integration still receives the outbound update when the source matches only one of them; a check that skipped every outbound sync whenever any source was set would not be caught.
